☕ THE LEAD

This holiday season, marketers aren't just battling for eyeballs; they're battling for agent-eyeballs. Agentic commerce is officially here, and it's set to reshuffle the entire economics of the web, especially for advertising. OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet and Google's AI Mode are pushing agent-led purchases, while Amazon is already blocking Meta's Muse AI agent from its site, showing how quickly the retail landscape is changing. Walmart's even letting customers cap agent spending, acknowledging that these AI shopping assistants are producing "notably different consumer behaviors." [S23][S4][S94]

This isn't some distant sci-fi future; it's Q4 2026, and brands *have* to figure out how their storytelling translates when an AI is doing the shopping. If your brand isn't thinking about how its value proposition, reviews, and product data will look when an AI is comparing options for a consumer (who might not even see your ad directly), you're already behind. The stakes are high: Meta's own Muse agent has reportedly been mixing up conversations and exposing private data, highlighting the privacy and trust challenges that come with letting AI agents handle our shopping. [S20][S23][S50] Marketers need to focus on clear, agent-optimized product data and trusted brand signals, because your next customer might be an algorithm.

📣 QUICK HITS

**Coca-Cola pivots away from AI-generated holiday ads after backlash.**
Remember the AI-generated ads that got mixed reviews? Coke heard the feedback and is now running "Enjoy Joy" spots featuring actual families and friends enjoying the holidays. Sometimes, human connection still beats generative AI, especially when it comes to brand perception. [S3]

**Instagram rolls out Amazon affiliate links for creators.**
Creators can now add up to 30 shoppable Amazon products per Reel, deepening the platform's play in social commerce. This is a massive win for creators looking to monetize and a clear signal for brands to lean into affiliate strategies with their content creators. [S9]

**Burger King's new campaign embraces its own flaws.**
Following earlier efforts to collect customer complaints, Burger King is now running a 60-second spot asking for feedback, directly addressing the need to improve the dining-room experience. It's a bold, transparent move that tries to turn customer complaints into a brand-building opportunity. [S8]

**Advertisers pause TikTok spend over CSAM investigation in Spain.**
Several major advertisers, including Santander and Moeve, have suspended activity on TikTok after reports of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) circulating on the platform. This highlights the ongoing brand safety challenges for platforms and the quick trigger advertisers have when trust is compromised. [S26]

🎯 THE PMM DESK

**Sonos kicks off Black Friday with up to 30% off speakers and soundbars.**
The audio giant is offering significant discounts, including $250 off the Arc Ultra soundbar and $60 off the Sonos Play, available through November 30th. For PMMs, this is a masterclass in seasonal pricing strategy, using anchor products to drive traffic and clear inventory during a peak shopping period. [S1]

**Google Gemini on Mac gains "computer use" capabilities.**
Gemini can now access local files and desktop apps on macOS to help users with multi-step tasks like filling forms or making presentations. This is a crucial product expansion that positions Gemini as a true productivity agent, requiring PMMs to clearly articulate the new workflow benefits and privacy controls to drive adoption. [S2][S48]

🧠 PMM 101

**The concept:** Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategy
**What it is:** A GTM strategy is a comprehensive plan outlining how a company will bring a new product or feature to market. It covers everything from identifying the target audience and crafting core messaging to defining sales channels, pricing, and the marketing activities needed to drive awareness and adoption.
**Why it matters:** A strong GTM ensures your product launches successfully, reaches the right customers, and achieves its business goals.
**See it today:** Google's launch of Gemini's "computer use" on Mac is a perfect example. Their GTM needs to clearly communicate *what* it does (multi-step tasks across apps), *who* it's for (Mac users seeking productivity boosts), and *how* it works (user-controlled access). [S2][S48]
**Try it:** Pick a new feature from an app you use daily. Outline what you think its GTM strategy would look like: Who is it for? What's the main benefit? How would you tell people about it?

🧩 PRODUCT CORNER

**Microsoft is sunsetting To Do in favor of Planner.**
Microsoft is consolidating its task management tools, effectively killing off the popular Wunderlist-turned-To Do app to unify tasks under Planner. This move highlights the tough product management decision-making involved in streamlining overlapping tools, even if it means alienating some loyal users. [S56]

🔧 TOOL DROP

**Adside** — A team of specialized AI agents that manage paid ads for you. [S107][S38]
Best for: Small to medium businesses or agencies looking to automate ad campaign optimization.
Free tier: No (Product Hunt page doesn't mention, implying paid).
Honest take: Potentially genuinely useful if it delivers on its promise of specialized agents, but AI ad management tools vary wildly in effectiveness. Definitely worth a trial to see if it beats a human.

⚡ SPEED ROUND

✨ Anthropic IPO'd at $111, valuing the company at $1.5 trillion despite an $80.7 billion net loss in H1 2026. Wild. [S54][S55][S66][S96]
🎮 GTA 6's official launch day has sparked a "work blackout" with 40 billion YouTube views pre-launch. [S25][S104]
📉 Walmart's global ad business saw its weakest growth in two years, up 25% YoY. [S18]
🔗 LinkedIn added "Sumbreak," its ninth in-stream game, as part of a push for user retention. [S32]
🍎 Apple's long-time VP of camera software engineering, Jon McCormack, retired last month. [S47]
🗣️ Elon Musk spent a record $445 million on midterm elections and now feels "pretty foolish." [S35][S90]
